items.title: Russia and Ukraine trade strikes on each other's capitals as Moscow signals readiness for talks
items.summary: France 24, CNN and NBC report that Russia hit Kyiv with missiles and drones on 21 to 22 October, hours after Putin agreed in principle, after meeting US envoy Steve Witkoff, to resume US-mediated trilateral talks, possibly after 10 November. Ukraine said at least 21 ballistic missiles were fired in three waves, and Moscow's mayor said hundreds of drones were headed for the region overnight. Casualty figures differ by source, so treat them as provisional.
items.why: A prolonged war keeps energy and commodity prices volatile and shapes sanctions and supply-chain risk that multinationals plan hiring around.

items.title: Putin's agreement to resume talks is in principle, with no date fixed
items.summary: The reports above say trilateral talks with Ukraine and the US could come after 10 November, and would be the first since February. Analysts quoted see no sign Russia has shifted its main positions.
items.why: A date would matter for markets, but the wording is still conditional.

items.title: India and Poland aim to double trade by 2030 and open a defence industry dialogue
items.summary: Following talks between PM Modi and Polish PM Donald Tusk in New Delhi on 22 October, the two sides set a target of doubling bilateral trade by 2030, agreed to a Defence Industry Dialogue and a counter-terrorism dialogue, and said Poland will join the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure. Cybersecurity, critical minerals and connectivity were also named as areas for cooperation. Tusk's visit runs from 21 to 23 October.
items.why: Bilateral trade targets open export and market-entry roles in engineering, defence supply chains and consumer goods that recruit MBAs.

items.title: India-Poland trade was 6.36 billion US dollars in 2025
items.summary: Revoi, citing official figures, puts 2025 bilateral trade at 6.36 billion dollars, the base for the 2030 doubling target.
items.why: A concrete base figure makes a target easier to judge.

items.title: Jio Platforms IPO sees strong institutional demand on day two while the market slips
items.summary: Business Standard reports the Rs 30,213 crore Jio Platforms IPO was subscribed 5.57 times on day two with qualified institutional buyers at 13.29 times, and The Week says the retail portion was fully subscribed even as the Sensex and Nifty fell. The Week puts the overall figure nearer 4.2 times, so the end-of-day tally is provisional. Business Standard's headline says the Sensex fell 460 points and the Nifty ended at 22,688. The issue closes on 23 October.
items.why: Record demand for an India IPO shows how much investors will pay for a consumer-tech brand story, which frames how marketers argue brand value.

items.title: Eternal's Q2 profit jumps 92 per cent to Rs 125 crore as Blinkit scales
items.summary: Deccan Herald and Indian Startup News report Eternal, the parent of Zomato and Blinkit, posted a September-quarter consolidated net profit of about Rs 125 crore, up from Rs 65 crore a year earlier, with revenue from operations of Rs 24,138 crore. Coverage says Blinkit earned Rs 184 crore and targets 3,500 stores. Cash fell by Rs 1,813 crore to Rs 16,475 crore.
items.why: Quick commerce is one of the fastest-growing employers of marketing, category and operations talent in India.

items.title: Canva launches Craft, its first in-house image generation model
items.summary: Digital Trends, Unite.AI and AI Weekly report that Canva released Craft on 22 October, trained on its own library of human-designed templates and working in two stages, a layout planning pass and a render pass, with output up to 2K across about 30 aspect ratios. It is open to all Canva users through Dream Lab and to developers via the API. Canva's claim of a fourth-place ranking on a design leaderboard is preliminary and self-reported.
items.why: Marketers will be expected to produce on-brand creative with tools like this, so knowing what they can and cannot do is now a basic skill.

items.title: Eternal announces Dark, a privacy-focused AI assistant planned for a 2026 launch
items.summary: Inc42 and Entrepreneur India report that Eternal's shareholder letter described Dark, an AI assistant that, the company says, keeps user conversation history in an encrypted memory it cannot read, aimed at founders, researchers and enterprises. Founder Deepinder Goyal said it would launch globally 'hopefully within 2026'. Outside commentary notes there is no launch date, pricing or demo yet and no independent audit of the privacy claim.
items.why: Privacy as a product promise is a positioning choice marketers and HR teams handling employee data will increasingly have to explain.
